finding: PersistentAgencyStore accepts only UnifiedDBResolution, checks only that the selected path is absolute and its parent directory exists, and opens sqlite3.connect(path). A missing target is therefore created by SQLite. No UnifiedDBFingerprint is required or bound, resolution.exists_at_resolution is not required, and no file device/inode/path identity is revalidated before write. The current restart test intentionally resolves a previously missing tempfile/unified.db and fingerprints it only after PersistentAgencyStore.persist has created/written it. This proves restart persistence but does not prove that the writer was bound to a pre-existing fingerprinted canonical UnifiedDB identity.

canonical_precedent.contract: CanonicalDeliveryStore requires both UnifiedDBResolution and UnifiedDBFingerprint, requires resolution.exists_at_resolution, requires fingerprint status SQLITE3_REGULAR_FILE, verifies resolved/fingerprinted real path plus device/inode identity, and opens with SQLite mode=rw so the writer never creates the database.

hypothesis: Without the same existing-file/fingerprint identity fence, WP206 can accidentally become an ad-hoc database bootstrap writer or write to a replaced/unfingerprinted SQLite target, weakening the single canonical UnifiedDB authority boundary.
counterhypothesis: A missing resolver-selected XDG_FRESH_TARGET can legitimately be the canonical fresh-install location, so creation itself is not necessarily a second authority. This counterhypothesis would require an explicit admitted bootstrap/schema authority granting WP206 the right to initialize that fresh database and bind its created identity before durable checkpoint credit. No such authority is present in the observed WP206 claim/source.
discriminator: Construct a UnifiedDBResolution whose target does not yet exist and whose exists_at_resolution is false; PersistentAgencyStore must fail closed unless a separately admitted canonical DB bootstrap contract is explicitly supplied.
For an existing target, require an exact UnifiedDBFingerprint and reject a path/file identity replacement between fingerprint and writer open.
Open the canonical writer with SQLite mode=rw rather than creation-capable sqlite3.connect(path), unless a distinct bootstrap authority is being tested.
Repeat the subprocess restart test against a pre-created/fingerprinted canonical test UnifiedDB and bind the fingerprint receipt identity into the integration evidence.
recommended_action: Treat this as a pre-acceptance fail-closed blocker for WP206 G1. Reuse the accepted CanonicalDeliveryStore identity-fence pattern or factor a shared canonical SQLite writer-open primitive; do not weaken F2-WP-100/F2-WP-103 authority boundaries merely to make the restart test green.
